en: Vimānavatthu: The Mansion of the Man,
Chapter on the Great Chariot (Mahārathavagga)
3. The Mansion of the Young Brahmin Chatta “He who is the most excellent among those who speak,
the Sakyan Sage, the Blessed One, who has accomplished what was to be done;”
One who has gone to the further shore,
endowed with power and energy— go for refuge to that Sugata.
He is free from passion, unshakable, and sorrowless.
The Dhamma is unconditioned and non-repulsive;
this sweet, skillful, and well-expounded Dhamma— come to it for refuge.
And where they say a gift yields great fruit—
among those four pairs of pure persons,
those eight individuals who are seers of the Dhamma—
Go for refuge to this Sangha.
Neither does the sun scorch so fiercely in the sky,
nor do the moon or Phussa shine [as brightly].
Since this incomparable, great radiance has appeared,
who indeed are you that have come from the triple heaven to the earth?
The rays of the light-maker cut through [the darkness].
His radiance extends for more than twenty-five yojanas;
he makes the night like day within his utterly pure,
stainless, and beautiful celestial mansion.
Variegated with many lotuses and white lilies,
strewn with various kinds of flowers,
and covered by a dustless, stainless net of gold.
Like the sun blazing in the sky,
[they shone] with their saffron and yellow robes, richly anointed with agallochum, yellow sandalwood, and sandalwood.
With skin resembling the color of gold,
like the sky filled with stars;
there were many men and women here of various complexions.
Here, the Sumanā flowers, adorned with ornaments,
waft a fragrant scent released by the wind;
they are spread out like refined gold and covered in fine gold.
Of what self-restraint is this the result?
By what fruit of karma have you been reborn here?
And how was this celestial mansion attained by you?
Immediately after that, being questioned, he spoke:
"Having encountered me here on the road, the Teacher himself, out of compassion, instructed this young brahmin."
"Having heard the Dhamma from you,
the most excellent jewel, I shall practice it," said Chatta.
"Go for refuge to the supreme and noble Conqueror."
"Likewise, O Bhante, regarding the Dhamma and the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, I did not say 'no' first;
afterwards, I acted exactly according to your word."
"Do not practice the various impurities of taking life;
for the wise have not praised lack of restraint toward living beings.
"So it is," I said first, venerable sir.
Afterwards, I acted exactly according to your word.
Do not think that what is guarded by another may be taken as "mine" if it has not been given.
"Venerable sir, I did not speak first;
I acted exactly according to your subsequent words.
Do not [speak thus] to those who protect others."
"She went to another's wife; this is ignoble"—
this was the first thing I said, venerable sir,
and afterwards I acted exactly according to those words.
"Do not speak falsely or otherwise,
for the wise do not praise false speech.
"I said 'No,' O Bhante, for the first time."
Afterwards, I acted exactly according to your words.
You should avoid all that intoxicant by which a person’s perception is lost.
"Venerable sir, I did not speak first;
I acted exactly according to your subsequent words.
Having performed the five training rules here,"
Having practiced according to the Dhamma of the Tathāgata,
I fell upon a double path among thieves;
they killed me there for the sake of my wealth.
"I remember this much merit;
beyond that, nothing else is known to me.
By virtue of that well-performed deed,"
He has arisen among the three worlds as one who seeks sensual pleasures.
Behold the fruit of practicing in accordance with the Dhamma:
his perception of [only] moments and instants.
Many of inferior conduct, looking upon me with envy as if at water, desire me;
behold this through my brief teaching.
I have gone to a happy destination and attained happiness;
and those who constantly listen to the Dhamma,
I believe they touch the secure state of the Deathless.
Even a small deed performed toward the Dhamma of the Tathāgata yields a vast and abundant result;
behold the umbrella [of honor] resulting from the merit one has made!
"It illuminates the earth just like the sun.
"What is this? What is wholesome?
What should we do?"—thus some, having come together, deliberate.
Having once again obtained this human state,
we dwell practicing the path, endowed with virtue;
the Teacher is our benefactor and is compassionate.
Thus, while I was thus present, the day passed by day after day.
Now that I have approached you, O you whose name is Truth,
have compassion on me so that we may hear the Dhamma once again.
Those who here abandon sensual lust, having abandoned the underlying tendency to lust for existence and delusion,
do not return again to a womb.
"For they have attained final Nibbāna and have become cooled.
Thus ends the third Vimāna, the *Chattamāṇavaka-vimāna*.
